about: The irrigation districts' canal dates for the canal season (season.py; README, 'The canal season'; the owner's decision 18). Empty until the owner asks for the lookups: each entry is one district's season as its own page states it, entered by hand, never scraped. Load it after every edit: python3 -m ingest canal-dates-load. One entry per district and season: id (lower case, unique), district (its name, as it gives it), canals (water.canal names, as the district names them, matched anywhere in the valley; 'branches': true adds the canals fed from them), optionally head_in (IDWR service-area names: only the named canals whose head lies in one) or canal_ids (water.canal ids: only those; they follow the builds) when a name selects canals of another district (the load lists every name that selects several, with their ids, lengths and service areas), on and off (the day water is turned in and the day it's shut off, 'YYYY-MM-DD', or with a time, 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' in Boise time; at least one; both in one calendar year), text (the district's words, a sentence at most), source (the page's URL), read (the day we read it, YYYY-MM-DD) and optionally republish (default yes: a date is a fact, cited). Within its year, an entry replaces IDWR's legal window on its canals: off before 'on', on from 'on' to 'off', off from 'off'. With no 'off' yet, the water runs to the end of the canal's legal season (IDWR's date, so that span is internal until the shut-off is entered). A later entry wins over an earlier one; a gauge (the New York Canal's BSEI1) wins over both. Example: {"id": "example-district-2027", "district": "Example Irrigation District", "canals": ["Example Canal"], "on": "2027-04-06", "off": "2027-10-15", "text": "Water will be turned into the canal on April 6.", "source": "https://example.org/notices", "read": "2027-03-20"}.
